subject: Mutual action: execution timetable & hosting lane commitment
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Claire Rogers <claire@greenfieldhealth.org>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial MAP + evaluation timetable — hosting lane question

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for a productive demo last week. I put together an initial mutual action timetable (attached) that lays out the evaluation steps we discussed, decision gates, and an indicative close timeline. The purpose of this note is to align on the hosting lane (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) so we can shape the evaluation environment and the timing for procurement items.

High level asks from our side:
- Pick a preferred hosting lane (hosted / dedicated / private) for the evaluation phase — this affects provisioning lead time.
- Confirm data residency requirements for the POC (US-only or US + EU?).
- Identify procurement contacts and any required legal/compliance docs (we've attached a SOC2 summary).

What I propose as a minimum evaluation plan (week numbers relative to start):
1) Week 0: Kickoff, credentials, small gen test against your worst-case profile (latency/cost targets).
2) Weeks 1–2: End-to-end integration with sample traffic, trace collection.
3) Week 3: Quality checks on prompt set, latency SLO verification.
4) Week 4: Decision workshop and procurement signoff target.

If Greenfield wants to evaluate both Dedicated and Private paths, we can run them in parallel, but it changes the procurement window (private can take 4–6 weeks for network and KMS work). Hosted is fastest to get results (48–72 hours to provision).

Attached: Greenfield_MUTUAL_ACTION_TIMETABLE_v2.xlsx (high-level milestones) and SOC2-Redwood-summary.pdf.

If you can confirm the hosting preference and the procurement contact by end of this week, we can lock milestones and target a firm close date.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
From: Claire Rogers <claire@greenfieldhealth.org>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 11:06:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Initial MAP + evaluation timetable — hosting lane question

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for sending this through — the timeline looks sensible. A few clarifying points from procurement and security:

1) Data residency: For the POC we need US-only processing and storage. If we move to prod, theres a high likelihood we will require EU controls (we'll flag later).
2) SOC2: The summary is helpful; procurement will want the full attestation and a contact for SOC evidence requests.
3) Hosting lanes: For speed-to-insight we prefer Hosted initially to validate model fit. However, given PHI/PII concerns and our security posture, we want a parallel feasibility assessment for Dedicated (predictable throughput) and Private (VPC + customer KMS). Can you outline the incremental lead times and a short cost delta for Dedicated vs Private?

Procurement contact: Procurement team is looping in Jessica Li (jessica.li@greenfieldhealth.org) — she will handle contract logistics and will reach out for redlines and PO timing.

Claire Rogers
Chief Product Officer
Greenfield Health

Quick internal plan proposal:
- Proceed with Hosted POC (48–72h provision). Configure with privacy-preserving defaults (disable telemetry, strict retention).
- Kick off Dedicated feasibility: estimate resource sizing, and provide: (a) throughput targets, (b) expected token volume 1M/day, (c) SLAs required. Expect ~2 weeks for cost and capacity confirmation (hardware allocation).
- Private feasibility: network & KMS review. Ask infra team for estimated network turnaround (typical 3–6 weeks depending on firewall/KMS).

Ben — can you draft a one-pager cost delta (hosted vs dedicated vs private) that we can share with procurement? Karthik — can you own the Dedicated sizing ask and collect any infra constraints from Greenfield (eg permitted IP ranges, KMS vendor)?

Quoting Claire below for convenience.
